abstract: Missense variant-effect predictors now provide proteome-scale estimates of amino acid substitution impact, but their outputs remain distributed across independent resources and are difficult to explore jointly with protein structural and human-variation context. We present MissenseDB, a residue-centric database integrating three architecturally distinct transformer-based predictors, AlphaMissense, VESM-3B, and VESPA, across the reviewed human proteome. MissenseDB contains 10 734 339 residue positions across 19 436 canonical human proteins, with complete three-predictor coverage for 19 434 proteins. Predictor outputs are linked to 211 731 UniProt-to-structure mappings, residue-level secondary-structure and molecular-context annotations, and Pfam domain membership, together with 59 851 HUMSAVAR missense variants enriched with population allele frequencies and ClinVar annotations. Raw predictor scores are provided together with empirically calibrated probabilities referenced to a common prior, on which a single decision threshold applies; on this calibrated scale all three predictors agree on ~75%-77% of pathogenic and benign variants. An interactive interface couples protein-wide sequence tracks with three-dimensional structural visualization and provides access to the complete 19-substitution landscape at individual residues. REST endpoints support protein-, residue-, and proteome-scale retrieval, while versioned relational database snapshots and a genomic coordinate lookup table enabling direct mapping from GRCh38 VCF coordinates to UniProt residues enable reproducible bulk analysis. MissenseDB is freely accessible without registration at https://biosig.lab.uq.edu.au/missense_db.
